Casual hotel with a cafe & a garden
Relaxed hotel offering mountain views, as well as a cafe, a garden & a meditation room.
On a tree-lined street, this laid-back hotel with views of the surrounding Himalayas mountains is off the NH505 national highway and 4 minutes' walk from Sakya Tangyud Monastery.
The simple, colourful rooms come with Wi-Fi access and en suite bathrooms. Upgraded rooms add TVs, tea and coffeemaking facilities, and/or mountain views.
Amenities include a cafe, a garden and a meditation room. Parking and bike storage are available, and there's also a generator.

Deyzor Kaza is much more than just a place to eat—it’s an experience. The food is absolutely delicious, with every dish feeling fresh, thoughtfully prepared, and full of flavor.

What truly makes this place special is the atmosphere. Every corner reflects the owner’s personal travel experiences, with décor, collectibles, and little details gathered from the many places they’ve explored. It gives the café a warm, authentic character and makes you feel like you’re stepping into someone’s travel journal rather than just another restaurant.

If you’re in Kaza, Deyzor is a must-visit for great food, a cozy vibe, and a space that tells a beautiful story through its design.

This place quietly offers you belonging. Almost like becoming part of something created with  intention and held together with immense love. Every corner carries its own story. You can feel that Karan and Kim have created a space where everyone can pause and breathe a little deeper. There is a certain kind of magick here that can't really be designed. And that same bit of magick is poured into every dish as well. It's something you absolutely shouldn't miss. There's also a thoughtfully curated bookstore where you can lose yourself for a while along with a lovely store with local handicrafts and produce to take a a small piece of Spiti home with you.
The Deyzor family welcomed me with such warmth. Rakesh, Bunty, and everyone on the team carry this place quietly and so effortlessly. In a landscape as humbling as Spiti, it's rare to find a place that feels just as expansive in heart.

We got the opportunity to experience finest of the hospitality from Karan and his wonderful team for a couple of days in Kaza. It is very hard to believe that they have created such a humble yet magnificent set up while providing an experience that befits all types of travellers. From the moment we stepped in, we could feel the warmth in every single interaction - be it our check in, room requirements, meals, casual chats etc. I am still astonished at how well their kitchen staff is trained - kudos to the people who served us chicken kiev and mutton tabrezi- they were out of this world! To imagine, we can get meals of such diverse geographies under one roof and that too perfected - it simply blew my mind.

Really appreciate the warm embrace of your setup- every single object reflects what you value. I loved spending time in the common area, such a perfect reading nook!

Nothing about our stay and interactions felt commercial- which unfortunately is the case with many travels these days. I absolutely look forward to making it to Deyzor again. Thank you for making our time in Kaza so wonderful, we remember it very fondly!

We stayed here for 4 days( October 2025) and overall it was a really good experience.

The entire hotel has a colorful, vibrant ambience, perfect for anyone who loves aesthetic spaces. Every corner is thoughtfully designed, which really adds to the charm of the place.

Convenient Location :  Around 200 mtrs from the main Market. Hospital is just like 100 mtrs from the property.
Dining : Fast service and good food. Drinks are also available on request.
Rooms : Premium rooms are definitely better in terms of space, natural light, and overall comfort. But yeah,  the standard rooms don’t offer much of a view, as the windows face a wall of the building, which can feel a bit closed. The owner was kind enough to upgrade our stay to a premium room for the first night.

Overall ambiance, hospitality, and vibe of the place make it a pleasant stay in Spiti.

Tip: Go for the premium rooms for a better experience!

I rarely leave reviews this bad, but the food here was genuinely awful. We ordered a few different items, and every single one was a massive disappointment:

Grilled Fish: Dripping in oil and incredibly greasy. It felt more like it was deep-fried in old oil than grilled.

Thukpa: This wasn't even Thukpa. It was just a bowl of random veggies with absolutely no soup and no noodles. Complete rip-off.

The "Special" Pizza: For a signature dish, it was a disaster. It had a foul, distinctively bad smell to it that made it completely unappetizing.

When a restaurant can't even get its own "specialty" right, you know something is seriously wrong in the kitchen. Subpar ingredients, zero care in preparation, and a total waste of money. Save your appetite and go literally anywhere else.

I’ve stayed at many many hotels/homestays but this place, is something else. It embodies Spiti but in ways that is not even close to a remote place like Spiti. The vibes, the walls, the decor, every single element here is as if it’s meant to be. Not forced but just there, a memento , a thank you note, a quote about Spiti, photographs, book shelves, raw items from nature. All this and more.

Karanbir, Rakesh, Bunty and team serve much more than just mere hospitality. They serve comfort, they give hope, they share stories and help create memories that you cannot let go for years to come. They take care of each one walking into those yellow doors, just like their own.

Thank you guys, for making @hoteldeyzor the comfort spot that we needed in the sub zero zone of Spiti.
